notes.title: Version 0.7.13
notes.content:
[b]Hello, friends![/b] We’ve got a major update for you—one that brings big changes and big potential… to break things. 😅 Please bear with us as we roll this out, and help us make Polylithic better by reporting any bugs or issues on our [url=https://www.discord.gg/polyperfect]Discord[/url] 

[h3]New Happiness System & Tribe Overview (Beta)[/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42930626/9ccceeb784edf9973a6f2cc69f6e0cef8115c2ab.jpg[/img]

[list]
[*] Global Happiness System added – affects the entire tribe.
[*] Food variety and surplus provide happiness boosts, rationing and scarcity cause drops.
[*] Each tribe member needs a place to stay and a bed to sleep on
[*] Housing Types: Stalk Cover, Hut, and House with different capacities and decoration support.
[*] Decorations now boost happiness (varies by housing).
[*] The decoration bonus applies only if people live in the house.
[*] Luxury Foods (bread, milk, meat) give happiness boosts.
[*] Tribe size now impacts happiness via a member penalty.
[*] Envy system added – members may get unhappy if housed unequally.
[*] Without proper food, housing, and decoration, happiness drops.
[*] At low happiness, tribe members may leave.
[*] Max sustainable tribe size (without issues): ~13 with full luxury setup.
[*] Overloading on poor housing types leads to limited happiness.
[*] New window for the tribe overview.
[*] New window for resources overview.
[/list]

The next step will be to add the positive and negative effects and balance the system more.

[h3]First Multiplayer Test![/h3]

[previewyoutube=FJ5lqFTwoBA;full][/previewyoutube]

We did our first multiplayer test today! 🎉 It's still a work in progress, but it’s already a blast (though sadly, my mic wasn’t recorded). If you want to help shape the future of Polylithic multiplayer and jump into beta testing with us, please let us know!

[h3]Performance Update[/h3]

[list]
[*] Loading the World chunks in the Sandbox mode
[*] Save and Load performance
[/list]

We will polish the new features in the upcoming small updates and continue to work on the new Fight and camera system, the New Campaign, and multiplayer, along with sandbox improvements, to get ready for the 1.0 release.

notes.title: 🐻 Animals and the best ways to hunt them 🦌
notes.content:
[h3]Howdy, Chiefs and Chieftainesses![/h3]

As you may know,  the paleo diet consists not just of vegetables, roots and the like but also animals. As per our last update, it’s now time to have a look at all prey available in the game, and best equipping yourself and the tribe to respond to their behavioural pattern and choosing how to tactile your ambushes!

[h2]🐔 Junglefowl [/h2]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42930626/463cb3d5ffe86291d8fdebb4f3212982f7b1349a.png[/img]
One the most common animals you first encounter when starting the game. Quick, nimble and easy to frighten away. You don’t need much strength in order to attack and It may well be one of the best target practice. It’s slow and vulnerable to all type of damage your weapons may provide: Blunt, Slashing, and Piercing.

With our Second Era updates, you will be able to tame the animal and have them in your settlement for eggs and meat. How exciting!

[h2] 🐇 Wild Rabbit[/h2]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42930626/af8733569d0f2b73d291147de6f9ee01058f84f5.png[/img]
Cute and just as easy to shy away once they spot you, these cuddly fellows speed away at the slightest provocation. It’s also rather easy to subdue and proves an easy source of meat at the start, and with all available weapons. Be sure to carve it right and you may be greeted with your first furs!

[h2] 🦌 Caribou Deer[/h2]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42930626/59fb81eafb4ba756532fed8061e0db24e37eaced.png[/img]
Requiring definitely more tactic than just brute force, deers are most susceptible to more advanced weapons with Piercing damage such as Javelins, Bone Spear, and Arrows. It would be best to circle them or drive them to a narrow pathway, cliffside or otherwise take their exit route out of the equation. They’re your first premium source of meat, bone and hides, as well as the only antlered animal in the game so far. 

[h2] 🐺 Dire Wolf[/h2]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42930626/37023090cdf6a549e408527638471c0393d9f0be.png[/img]
Congrats, you just crossed paths with the first predator in the game! Beware their sharp fangs and claws as wolves attack you on sight and their key advantage is numbers. Circling their victim, they will aim to tire you out and make sure you cannot draw distance to fire Piercing weapons at them. Be sure to bring your tribe along  to fight back, and persevere. 
Also, remember to fetch some meat  from your previous hunt – thanks to our newest update, you will be able to tame  them into loyal hunting companion!

[h2] 🐗 Wild Boar[/h2]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42930626/7b67179b04e041e7597a1af145b666ba1eebfce0.png[/img]
This battle will be legendary! Boars are small, nimble and definitely ferocious in guarding their forest territories – though small, they may be of the toughest enemies to master! Evade their sharp tusks, roll away and remember that their pursuit of you doesn’t end before you either run away or you defeat them in combat. They are resistant to mere Blunt or Slashing damage thanks to their thick skin.
Their bodies offer fat that you can use in crafting recipes, and once seduced with some treats, they are happy to join your growing farm.

[h2] 🐂 Aurochs[/h2]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42930626/670c130d55fc374adbdc41db41799300b511bf56.png[/img]
Thought to be the ancestors of today’s cattle, aurochs are stoic animals – that is, until they spot you trying to come closer to the herd. Once seen, they are guarding themselves to death and will charge at you without provocation. Approach with caution and only once you are a capable hunter – their hides make them more resistant to early stage weapons, and attacking them requires good communication with the tribe as direct Blunt damage doesn’t do much harm.

Bribe them with food, and you can start your cattle empire back at the camp, providing you with meat, milk, antlers and more!

[h2] 🐯 Tiger[/h2]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42930626/d979e6e29b1a904745ab80c11557574d77e6488a.png[/img]
The majestic beast that for sure hunted our ancestors’ nightmares! Beware this predator when alone as it will attack on sight and will not stop before either of you is dead, or you successfully evade it beyond its interest and sight. Nimble and a master hunter using their paws and sharp teeth, it’s best to rear clear of its territory before you get experience and bring your tribe people up to speed and same level of weapon mastery as your character. Picking up Blades and Piercing weapons are your best choice against them.

[h2] 🐻Brown Bear[/h2]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42930626/006ee5e152d46de4705a7487b0d1e31f5ca2a4f9.png[/img]
Definitely not the friendly Yogi bear but rather a deadly machine! Bears, just like tigers, will attack on sight and will not stop unless you best them, or run away. Remember, they are tougher and more menacing opponents as Slashing or Blunt weapons do little against their thick furs. Due to their size and magnitude, their corpses once carved offer you the most meat, bone, sinews, fat and fur, compared to previous types of animals.

[h2] 🐘 Mammoth[/h2]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42930626/e32d762d1869bc7ce17cc0edbdb4e022bcbef219.png[/img]
Legendary, woolly and deadly! Mammoths used to roam the earth thousands of years ago and you can definitely see why they were the prize hunting animals for our ancestors. Prepare to be stomped on, charged at, and pierced with sharp tusks – this particular animal fights with all their might, and they will not go easy on you. Ready your best weapons and combine different damage types against their ferocious attacks, as their weaknesses do not lie in one single type of weapons but rather tenacity and tribe cooperation.

Mammoths are the sole source of ivory for the game which you require in the later stages of your tribe to produce figurines out of polished ivory. 

We hope that this quick repertoire of the animals and best tactics on how to approach them aid you in making your tribes prosper and flourish! Tune in for our next updates and understanding the ins and outs of the low poly world of Polylithic!

[h3]Many thanks and may the Sun bless your steps!
Polyperfect Team [/h3]

notes.title: 🏹 Hunting tactics - what to do to get your next meal?
notes.content:
[h3]Howdy, Chiefs and Chieftainesses![/h3]

As per our latest update and the beautiful road of the last 6 months, our dev team is busy tweaking and bettering the second era of the game. Centred all around farming, cultivating the land and having animals of your very own to look after – oh yes, that chicken coop will definitely come in handy!

In the meantime, for all those getting into the game and those doing migration, let’s have a look at what made up the palaeolithic diet the way it was. Not just gathering but when the Gods aligned their divine wills: hunting!

[h1] 🏹 Hunting tactics 🏹 [/h1]

[h3][b] 🤫 Stalking[/b][/h3]
This tactic is all about silently following your prey and remaining in the shadows before the perfect moment to strike happens. Best to use against slow-moving animals and definitely worthwhile to lock your target once you have to burst from your crouched position.

[previewyoutube=OUHXdE7ltXk;full][/previewyoutube]

[h3][b] ⚔️ Pushing, flushing and driving[/b][/h3]
Best to implement as a group tactic with your fellow tribe people as it relies on moving the target or herd towards a predestined location, hopefully one that enables you to deal with the prey immediately. That includes driving animals towards cliffs, awaiting tribe members at the ready with their weapons, or using the terrains to your advantage, whether valleys or open grassy areas that make aiming your javelins easier and more reliable.

[previewyoutube=5Cz-vc2DdaU;full]https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=5Cz-vc2DdaU
[/previewyoutube]

[h3][b] 🎯 Stand or blind hunting[/b][/h3]
One of the tactics that persevered over the ages, relying on stillness and tricking animals into thinking you are a natural part of their environment because of the lack of movement, camouflage, and more! A lot of today’s hunters rely on this method and the booths are iconic parts of the landscape on the outskirts of forests.


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42930626/d0431a4eb4d7aca9eecc6d9fc8dbb772299181d7.jpg[/img]
[url=https://pl.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ambona_%28myślistwo%29]Source: Wikipedia [/url]

[h3][b] 🍓 Baiting[/b][/h3]
Using meat, berries or any other delicacies in order to lure animals. In our game, it’s possible to use this technique in order to domesticate a friendly and loyal friend to aid your hunts – check out our future updates for further details!

[previewyoutube=oWtGqpVff40;full]https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=oWtGqpVff40[/previewyoutube]

[h3][b] 🏃 Persistence, exhaustion or long distance hunting[/b][/h3]
The old and tried method of tiring down animals and relying that just because we can hardly catch our breath and our stamina runs low, theirs will deplete over time as well! It is speculated that this particular method allowed our ancestors to survive and evolve over time to build the advantage over our prey.

[previewyoutube=826HMLoiE_o;full][/previewyoutube]

You may be pleasantly surprised that our ancestors used the terrains just as much to their advantage as you, players of the game, can do! Some of the strategies survive throughout the eons and hundreds of years, having evolved into the style known by modern hunters across America, Europe, and beyond.


[h3]Many thanks, and may the Sun bless your steps!
Polyperfect Team[/h3]

We added a new Sandbox Mode with an automatically generated map and content, so now you can experience prehistoric ages with infinite fun without all those story quests. On top of it, there is a Creative mode where you can try all the new stuff we are adding to a game.

notes.title: 🔪 Weapons - key recipes, stats, and fighting styles
notes.content:
[h3]Howdy, Chiefs and Chieftainesses![/h3]

Now that we have a good menu of the animals available for hunting, covered the basics of tactics and how to use them against each of the prey types, let’s take a careful look at [b]the Weapons[/b]. Why, how and when to produce each type, and which hunting levels mean what.


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42930626/d03f4a1e94ef71a144b67218de056299f0e5e5a2.gif[/img]

However, before you process further, be sure to equip yourselves with the very first tool that makes crafting possible.  With its name leaving much to the imagination, [b][h2] Chopper[/h2][/b] was our ancestors’ Swiss Knife without a doubt.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42930626/736334b3f4ca93a66e5e011d4fc5e06bd39a1ca2.png[/img]

Chopping, carving up animals, creating first weapons and so much more – be sure to [b]create it from 2 Rocks[/b], and equip it on your character as soon as possible while following the in-game tutorial.
 
[h2][b]Club[/b][/h2]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42930626/65b4752f1a5da4740487e6dd983e4d8d453ac9b7.png[/img]
Your very first proper weapon, made of out [b]wooden Logs[/b] which you transform thanks to the [b]Chopper.[/b] Good at whacking down fowls and rabbits, dealing [i]Blunt damage[/i], but not very effective against bigger animals.

[h2][b]Torch[/b][/h2]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42930626/dd0422920cc93c035a124f19fc530d8728ffc7b6.png[/img]
Very first source of light, warmth, and danger – all in one! Gather some [b]Logs and Stalks[/b], and combine those at the [b]Camp Fire.[/b] It will burn and set your target on [i]fire[/i], so beware!

 
[h2][b]Stone Mallet[/b][/h2]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42930626/1efe65a4f733eb9b5e8affee1af7de7671457c77.png[/img]
In order to unlock it, you have to level up your skills, and [b]open the second stage of the technology tree[/b]. Constructed from [b]a Rock, a Log, and some Strings[/b], with the help of a [b]Chopper,[/b] the Mallet allows you not only to [b]hunt, but also build and construct[/b]. It is your second [i]Blunt[/i] melee weapon, with high damage.
 
[h2][b]Stone Axe[/b][/h2]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42930626/ca80c3a5ae590aa3b063013c70daed3dba7ae41d.png[/img]
Another more advanced tool that leads the secret life of a weapon. Its recipe requires [b]very similar compounds just like [b]the Mallet[/b], swapping Rocks for Flints[/b]. When equipped, you can try picking on bigger animals than deers, and chiselling off rocks for improved recipes. This is your first [i]Slashing[/i] weapon, and whose wounds [i]bleed[/i].
 
[h2][b]Javelin[/b][/h2]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42930626/ac1f598894984f58e49b73786290b7c8273216ed.png[/img]
Primitive, gaunt and bare minimum – here’s your [b]very first melee weapon that works at range[/b] as well! As with all crafting recipes, you need better tools now to prepare it, meaning [b]Stone Axe rather than the Chopper.[/b] Use it against animals that are more susceptible to [i]Piercing damage[/i], and  those fleeing as soon as they see you. In close combat, it’s not that effective.
 
[h2][b]Bone Spear[/b][/h2]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42930626/e377be71dfd9841e5e3b0656a454f1751e977ee3.png[/img]
Well, well, well! Look at this beauty of a bone-crowned spear – once you are more versed in crafting, you can be privy to [b]more advanced ranged weapons like this.[/b] Iconic, and doubling also as a [b]tool in crafting recipes[/b], this spear is more durable and will aid you against more vicious, higher-level predators, offering better [i]Piercing damage[/i]. You can also [b]knock back your enemies [/b]once you equip it, however – it’s useless in direct melee combat.
 
[h2][b]Blade[/b][/h2]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42930626/6917d03a755675df907d80ac61e8762ce37e52ae.png[/img]
Cut, strike, and evade! The mother of today’s knives, [b] the Blade [/b]requires more advanced technology and finesse in its production, and a [b]Grinding Stone to sharpen its Bone[/b]. Be sure to use it in close-ranged combat for[i] Slashing damage [/i]against smaller, and less tenacious animals. Unnless, of course, you are proficient at dodging and rolling, then this weapon may very well prove your favourite against any elements! It is also an [b]advanced crafting tool[/b] and will help you with preparation for the final weapon of the game.
 
[h2][b]Bow[/b][/h2]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42930626/d39ddfb8327744f059865fe06b0c68cbf464b4fe.png[/img]
And finally, crem de la crème of our armoury. Improved rather in a cosmetic manner than functional over centuries well until today, the bow and its arrows allow you to comfortably hunt all small and big animals, and deal [i]Piercing damage[/i].

[b]Blade is required to process Sinews instead of Strings[/b] for its production.

[h3]🎯 To summarize, we have [b][u]3 Technological Levels[/u][/b] [/h3]that you have to keep in mind when producing weapons and crafting tools:
[b][olist]
[*] Levallois – [i]Chooper, Camp Fire[/i]
[*] Mousterian – [i]Stone Axe[/i]
[*] Animal Processing – [i]Stone Axe, Grinding Stone, Blade[/i]
[/olist][/b]
There are also [b]dedicated Workstations [/b]that you unlock over time and mastering crafting recipes, but that is a tale for another update and introducing you further to key resources of the game and what to best use them for – stay tuned!

[h3]Many thanks, and may the Sun bless your steps!
Polyperfect Team[/h3]

notes.title: 🥩🌾Scavenging, food sourcing and where inspiration strikes
notes.content:
[h3]Howdy, Chiefs and Chieftainesses![/h3]

Have you ever wondered what the early humans did before the great leap into the wide unknown world of agriculture, tending to their very own plots of land to farm crops and vegetables?

[h2]Hunting, foraging, and scavenging, of course![/h2]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42930626/69fa227587921022c3236700c4d6fa2edf384e60.gif[/img]

There are many contradictory theories surrounding the dawn of humanity, and our game showcases one of them – first focusing on using the terrain to its best advantage by foraging for berries, roots, and any materials useful in perfecting weapons and further advancing the tribe. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42930626/7b5f34ede793f410da9aef6a3644858759a84af3.jpg[/img] 
[i]Wikipedia: Buffalo Hunters[/i]


Within the game itself, [b]food affects the status of your character [/b]and the tribe members tremendously – 3 statuses are impacted and whose maintenance is key to securing your survival. 
[list]
[*] [b]WELL-FED[/b] means that over-time healing gets triggered and your Stamina recovery rate is added; a food bonus gets applied to the given character
[*] [b]NO STATUS/EQUILIBRIUM[/b] provides no healing and Stamina recovers at normal rate; food bonus applied
[*] [b]STARVING [/b]provides an incentive to start hunting or gathering resources as soon as possible as your health decreases steadily before dropping to 25 HP. Your characters get a speed bonus to help find food sources but beware! Your stamina still gets affected and its recovery rate is decreased significantly. 
[/list]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42930626/bda407d83f3eaf0ea63a47f5267382b89f69d4a1.png[/img]

Food comes in many shapes, sizes, and polygons! From the humble berry, nuts, and succulent tree roots to juicy ribs and steaks – however, watch out and learn the ropes of watching the fire, the latter may be much more nutritious and tasty when heated up!

Migrations and changes in surroundings enabled our ancestors to perfect the equipment needed to actually aim at dominating meat sources such as caribou, chickens, all the way to mammoths – and later on, decide whether staying in one place and building a sustainable settlement may be the best move forward. 
 
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42930626/61df493a18f9177c2e016e4469654cc94ea609b2.png[/img]
But that is a tale for another day! In the meantime, here you can see a WIP for the household in the farming era, the second big part of our game.

Face the world of the paleolithic and archaic revolution that introduced us all to the lifestyle that changed the fate of humanity forever – and led us all this way to iron ore, steam, computing, and AI!

Strap on and let’s start the ride!
Polyperfect Team

notes.title: Version 0.4.1
notes.content:
Hello fellow tribe members. The new year is here along with version 0.4! This might not seem that much of a change but huge things are happening in the backend of the game allowing for the 2nd era of farming.

[list]
[*] Alterations to terrain, down to every blade of grass, are now saved in preparation for the farming era
[*] Trees and boulders now have their health and state saved by the scene
[*] Terrain remains persistent when traveling far away and coming back
[*] Terrain will be reset if loading data from a version of the game with a different generation
[*] Improved performance for a large number of mobs
[*] Reduced VRAM usage by ≈500MB
[*] Adjusted spawn rate of rocks
[*] Wheat now spawns in the world
[*] Additional points of interest have been added throughout the map
[*] Fixed various issues in the terrain
[*] Some inaccessible items added for super secret testing
[*] Small Trees and nut trees can be chopped now
[*] Small visual improvements
[/list]
As always, If you encounter any problems, please let us know!


[h2]Future updates[/h2]

What you can expect in the upcoming updates? The team is now focused on laying the foundation for the farming era that introduces the player to new technologies. Through this, the player will be able to use animals to produce more resources, cultivate the land, and hence start proper production chains.


[img]https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/603a768ef4a6a57df7ea3ab9/066df880-7aab-4351-ad1b-a4e64655e7b5/polylithic_10.png[/img]

The player is expected to settle down, build up their base, employ more NPCs to their tribe, explore the map, and follow up the story quest.


[img]https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/603a768ef4a6a57df7ea3ab9/886720ff-6bc6-4b0e-b676-dc579ab616a0/image+%281%29.png[/img]


The main areas we will be focusing on now are modular building, farming, and taming animals. Later on, we are also planning to introduce a Season System with a Winter / Summer cycle for more fun and challenging gameplay along with the sandbox mode. 


[img]https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/603a768ef4a6a57df7ea3ab9/21d6c9de-5705-4958-8a78-39c4c4166457/quests.PNG?format=2500w[/img]


We will be also adding new special NPCs and their fun questlines to the game world with continuous stories after each migration and some rewards. 

[b]Lastly, we are in the process of looking for help with more advanced game design a system balance.[/b]

notes.title: This new indie game is Valheim, but prehistoric
notes.content:
Polylithic caught my eye for a variety of reasons, from its vibrant color scheme to its unique premise. The indie game looks to be bringing a lot to the crafting-survival table with its Paleolithic Age setting. After thrusting you into the role of a tribal leader, Polylithic has you fight through a mysterious epidemic to help your people not only survive but also thrive. The strange sickness is not your only obstacle though, as the environment can be harsh and you'll need to work to keep your tribe fed, happy, and growing.
